newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt bank backs first open-ended securities fund.
newsitem.headline: Egypt bank backs first open-ended securities fund.

text.p: Egypt's Banque Misr and the Gulf Arab Investment Company have launched the first open-ended offshore fund to invest in Egyptian securities, an official close to the deal told Reuters on Monday.

The fund is called the Egyptian Growth Investment Company Limited and is managed by Concord Misr Investments, a joint-venture firm between New York-based Concord International Investments and the state-owned commercial bank.
The official, who refused to be named, said the fund's agents had raised close to $100 million and that it would be listed within a few weeks in Guernsey.
"This fund is the sole result of the Middle East and North Africa Conference," he said, referring to an internationl economic conference which took place in Cairo last November.
"We started work right after the meeting when there was a large appetite for Egypt," he added.
Local institutions Misr International Bank and Misr Romanian Bank as well as international securities houses HSBC James Capel and Nomura International Plc are selling and placing agents for the fund.
The fund can invest in listed and unlisted Egyptian securities as well as depository receipts and stocks the government will privatise.
There are several local and close-ended offshore funds that deal in Egyptian equities, which have currently attractive price-to-earning ratios of 12 to 13.
The Egyptian stock exchange has also risen in January to its highest level ever and brokers forecast more cash inflows will push the market even higher.

Last year, Concord and the state's National Bank of Egypt set up the $46 million Concord Fund, which was promoted by HSBC James Capel. SBC Warburg and Lazard Freres raised $74 million for the Egypt Trust and local brokerage EFG-Hermes helped raise $43 million for the Egypt Fund.
